newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Test offers NZers on-line supermarket shopping.
newsitem.headline: Test offers NZers on-line supermarket shopping.

text.p: Online Retail Systems Ltd on Tuesday announced it was trialling home shopping services via the Internet.
In the initial closed test, which will involve 80 Auckland customers, the customers will be able to order supermarket goods on-line from their homes and have the goods delivered within hours.
Online Retail Systems' owner Andrew Faris described the service, called "The Mall", as ground-breaking.

He said the partners for the closed test represented leaders in their fields. Woolworths is the retailer whose product line will be available from the online store, and New Zealand Post's courier service, Courier Post, will deliver the goods.
The Bank of New Zealand will facilitate payment for the groceries, and Telecom Internet Services will host The Mall on its XTRA site.
Faris said Online's aim was to have supermarket home shoppers make three out of four shops via The Mall.
The test will last 8-12 weeks and will be followed by a more comprehensive test of 500 customers before providing full public access.
